⇒ 87,500 = (5 / 13) × 0.7P

⇒ 87,500 × 13 = 3.5P

⇒ 11,37,500 = 3.5P

⇒ P = 11,37,500 ÷ 3.5

⇒ P = ₹3,25,000

∴ The correct answer is ₹325000.

Additional Information

Partnership Profit Sharing Rule

Profit is divided in the ratio of (Investment × Time). If time is same, Profit Ratio = Investment Ratio.

Distributed vs Reinvested Profit

Total Profit = Amount Reinvested + Amount Distributed among partners.

Working Partner vs Sleeping Partner

A working partner may receive an extra commission or salary from the profit before the remaining profit is distributed in the investment ratio.

questions.question: Working alone A can do the task in 27 hours and B can do it in 54 hours. Find C's share (in Rs) if A, B and C get paid Rs. 4,320 for completing a task in 12 hours on which they worked together.
questions.questionHtml: Working alone A can do the task in 27 hours and B can do it in 54 hours. Find C's share (in Rs) if A, B and C get paid Rs. 4,320 for completing a task in 12 hours on which they worked together.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of work/efficiency: A : B : (A+B+C) = 1/27 : 1/54 : 1/12

Multiplying by LCM 108: A = 4, B = 2, (A+B+C) = 9

Efficiency of C = 9 − (4 + 2) = 3

C's share = (C's efficiency ÷ Total efficiency) × Total wage = (3 ÷ 9) × 4320

C's share = 4320 ÷ 3 = 1440

∴ The correct answer is ₹1440.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by A = 27 hours

Time taken by B = 54 hours

Time taken by A, B, and C together = 12 hours

Total amount paid = ₹4,320

Formula Used:

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Share of a person ∝ Efficiency (when time of working is same for all)

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
A 27 108 (LCM) 108 ÷ 27 = 4
B 54 108 ÷ 54 = 2
A + B + C 12 108 ÷ 12 = 9

Calculations:

⇒ Efficiency of (A + B + C) = 9

⇒ Efficiency of A = 4

⇒ Efficiency of B = 2

⇒ Efficiency of C = Efficiency of (A + B + C) − Efficiency of (A + B)

⇒ Efficiency of C = 9 − (4 + 2) = 3

⇒ Ratio of efficiency A : B : C = 4 : 2 : 3

⇒ Total ratio units = 4 + 2 + 3 = 9 units

⇒ 9 units = ₹4,320

⇒ 1 unit = 4320 ÷ 9 = ₹480

⇒ C's share = 3 × 480 = ₹1,440

∴ The correct answer is ₹1440.

Additional Information

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in the ratio of work done by each individual. If they work for the same amount of time, the wage ratio is the same as the efficiency ratio.

Efficiency Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a task. Efficiency = 1 ÷ Time.

Total Work Concept

Total work is usually assumed as the LCM (Least Common Multiple) of the individual times to simplify efficiency calculations into integers.

questions.question: If A had worked alone he would have taken 63 hours to do the task. What is B's share, if A and B work together on a task finishing it in 36 hours and they get paid Rs. 5,950 for it?
questions.questionHtml: If A had worked alone he would have taken 63 hours to do the task. What is B's share, if A and B work together on a task finishing it in 36 hours and they get paid Rs. 5,950 for it?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Efficiency ratio of A to (A + B) = (1/63) : (1/36) = 36 : 63 = 4 : 7.

Since total efficiency is 7 and A is 4, B's efficiency = 7 − 4 = 3 units.

Ratio of shares A : B = 4 : 3 (as they work together for the same time).

B's share = (3 ÷ 7) × 5950 = 3 × 850 = ₹2550.

∴ The correct answer is ₹2550.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by A alone = 63 hours

Time taken by (A + B) together = 36 hours

Total payment = ₹5,950

Formula Used:

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Share of wages = (Individual Efficiency × Time) / Total Work. When time is constant, share ∝ Efficiency.

Person Hours Total Work (LCM) Efficiency
A 63 252 4
A + B 36 7

Calculations:

⇒ Efficiency of B = Efficiency of (A + B) − Efficiency of A

⇒ Efficiency of B = 7 − 4 = 3

⇒ Since they work together for the whole duration, wages are divided in the ratio of their efficiencies.

⇒ Ratio of Share (A : B) = 4 : 3

⇒ Total ratio units = 4 + 3 = 7 units

⇒ 7 units = ₹5,950

⇒ 1 unit = 5950 ÷ 7 = ₹850

⇒ B's share = 3 × 850 = ₹2550

∴ The correct answer is ₹2550.

Additional Information

Work and Wages Principle

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the work done by each individual. If persons work for the same amount of time, the wage ratio is the same as the efficiency ratio.

Efficiency and Time

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a piece of work. E1 × T1 = E2 × T2 = Total Work.

Combined Work Rate

If A takes 'a' days and B takes 'b' days, together they take (a × b) ÷ (a + b) days to complete the task.

questions.question: Working together A, B and C can complete a task in 12 days. A and B can do the task in 55 days and 66 days respectively if they worked alone. In how many days can C do the task if he worked alone?
questions.questionHtml: Working together A, B and C can complete a task in 12 days. A and B can do the task in 55 days and 66 days respectively if they worked alone. In how many days can C do the task if he worked alone?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Assume Total Work = LCM of (12, 55, 66) = 660 units.

Combined efficiency (A + B + C) = 660 ÷ 12 = 55 units/day.

Efficiency of A = 660 ÷ 55 = 12 units/day; Efficiency of B = 660 ÷ 66 = 10 units/day.

Efficiency of C = (A + B + C) − (A + B) = 55 − (12 + 10) = 33 units/day.

Time taken by C = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of C = 660 ÷ 33 = 20 days.

∴ The correct answer is 20 days.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by (A + B + C) working together = 12 days

Time taken by A alone = 55 days

Time taken by B alone = 66 days

Formula Used:

Total Work = Efficiency × Time taken

Efficiency of C = Efficiency of (A + B + C) − Efficiency of A − Efficiency of B

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
A + B + C 12 660 55
A 55 12
B 66 10

Calculations:

⇒ Efficiency of (A + B) = 12 + 10 = 22 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of C = Efficiency of (A + B + C) − Efficiency of (A + B)

⇒ Efficiency of C = 55 − 22 = 33 units/day

⇒ Time taken by C alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of C

⇒ Time taken by C alone = 660 ÷ 33

⇒ Time taken by C alone = 20 days

∴ The correct answer is 20 days.

Additional Information

Combined Work Formula

If individuals take x, y, and z days respectively, the together time T is given by 1/T = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z.

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a task (E ∝ 1/T) when work is constant.

LCM Method for Work

Choosing the LCM of given time periods as the total work avoids handling complex fractions during calculation.

questions.question: B would have taken 10 hours more than what A would have taken to complete a task if each of them worked alone. Working together they can complete the task in 12 hours. How many hours would B take to do 50% of the task?
questions.questionHtml: B would have taken 10 hours more than what A would have taken to complete a task if each of them worked alone. Working together they can complete the task in 12 hours. How many hours would B take to do 50% of the task?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For a combined time of 12 hours, standard work pairs are (20, 30) or (15, 60).

The condition states B takes 10 hours more than A, which perfectly matches the (20, 30) pair.

Calculated total time for B = 30 hours.

Time required for B to complete 50% of the task = 30 × 0.5 = 15 hours.

∴ The correct answer is 15 hours.

Alternate Method

Given: Combined time (A + B) = 12 hours; B = A + 10 hours.

Formula: 1 ÷ A + 1 ÷ B = 1 ÷ Total Time

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
A 20 60 3
B 30 2

Calculations:

⇒ Let A take x hours, then B takes (x + 10) hours.

⇒ 1/x + 1/(x + 10) = 1/12

⇒ (x + 10 + x) ÷ (x × (x + 10)) = 1/12

⇒ 12(2x + 10) = x2 + 10x

⇒ 24x + 120 = x2 + 10x

⇒ x2 − 14x − 120 = 0

⇒ (x − 20)(x + 6) = 0

⇒ x = 20 (Time cannot be negative)

⇒ Time taken by B = 20 + 10 = 30 hours

⇒ Time for 50% work by B = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 hours

∴ The correct answer is 15 hours.

Additional Information

Work Rate and Time

The rate of work is inversely proportional to the time taken. If a person completes work in T hours, their efficiency is 1/T per hour.

Combined Work Formula

For two individuals A and B with times ta and tb, the combined time T is given by T = (ta × tb) ÷ (ta + tb).

Efficiency Ratio

Ratio of time taken by A and B is the inverse of the ratio of their efficiencies. If time ratio is x:y, efficiency ratio is y:x.

questions.question: Giving two successive discounts of 20% is same as giving one discount of ________ %.
questions.questionHtml: Giving two successive discounts of 20% is same as giving one discount of ________ %.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Successive Discount Formula = x + y − (x × y)/100

Given: x = 20 and y = 20

Net Discount = 20 + 20 − (20 × 20)/100

Net Discount = 40 − 400/100

Net Discount = 40 − 4 = 36

∴ The correct answer is 36%.

Alternate Method

Given:

First discount rate (d1) = 20%

Second discount rate (d2) = 20%

Formula Used:

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × (1 − d1/100) × (1 − d2/100)

⇒ Let the Marked Price (MP) be ₹100.

⇒ Price after first discount of 20% = 100 − (20% of 100)

⇒ Price after first discount = 100 − 20 = ₹80.

⇒ Price after second discount of 20% = 80 − (20% of 80)

⇒ Price after second discount = 80 − 16 = ₹64.

⇒ Total discount given = MP − Final Price

⇒ Total discount = 100 − 64 = ₹36.

⇒ Equivalent Discount Percentage = (36/100) × 100 = 36%.

∴ The correct answer is 36%.

Additional Information

Successive Discount for Three Rates

For three successive discounts a%, b%, and c%, the net discount is calculated by applying the formula twice or using: Net Discount = 100 − [100 × (1 − a/100) × (1 − b/100) × (1 − c/100)].

Relation between MP, CP, Profit and Discount

The ratio of Marked Price to Cost Price can be expressed as: MP/CP = (100 + Profit%)/(100 − Discount%).

Successive Percentage Change

The net percentage change for two successive changes of x% and y% is given by [x + y + (xy/100)]%. For discounts, x and y are taken as negative.

questions.question: A retailer marks up his goods by 150% and offers 40% discount. What will be the selling price (in Rs.) if the cost price is Rs. 800?
questions.questionHtml: A retailer marks up his goods by 150% and offers 40% discount. What will be the selling price (in Rs.) if the cost price is Rs. 800?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

SP = CP × (Multiplier for Markup) × (Multiplier for Discount)

Multiplier for 150% markup = (100 + 150)/100 = 2.5

Multiplier for 40% discount = (100 − 40)/100 = 0.6

SP = 800 × 2.5 × 0.6 = 2000 × 0.6 = 1200

∴ The correct answer is ₹1200.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost Price (CP) = ₹800

Markup % = 150%

Discount % = 40%

Formula Used:

Marked Price (MP) = CP + (Markup % of CP)

Selling Price (SP) = MP − (Discount % of MP)

Calculations:

⇒ CP = ₹800

⇒ Markup = 150% of 800 = (150/100) × 800 = ₹1200

⇒ MP = CP + Markup = 800 + 1200 = ₹2000

⇒ Discount = 40% of MP = (40/100) × 2000 = ₹800

⇒ SP = MP − Discount = 2000 − 800 = ₹1200

∴ The correct answer is ₹1200.

Additional Information

Net Profit Percentage

Net Profit % = Markup % − Discount % − (Markup % × Discount %)/100. In this case: 150 − 40 − (150 × 40)/100 = 110 − 60 = 50%.

Relation between CP and MP

MP/CP = (100 + Profit %)/(100 − Discount %). This formula helps find the required markup to gain a specific profit after offering a discount.

Effective Discount

For successive discounts d1 and d2, the single equivalent discount is (d1 + d2 − (d1 × d2)/100)%.

questions.question: On television of brand A, the discount is 25% and on television of brand B, the discount is 40%. The price of B after discount is Rs. 2,250 greater than the price of A after discount. What is the marked price of A (in Rs.) if the marked price of B is Rs. 35,000?
questions.questionHtml: On television of brand A, the discount is 25% and on television of brand B, the discount is 40%. The price of B after discount is Rs. 2,250 greater than the price of A after discount. What is the marked price of A (in Rs.) if the marked price of B is Rs. 35,000?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

SP of Brand B = 60% of MP = 0.60 × 35000 = ₹21,000

SP of Brand A = SP of Brand B − 2250 = 21000 − 2250 = ₹18,750

MP of Brand A = SP ÷ (100% − 25%) = 18750 ÷ 0.75

MP of Brand A = 18750 × (4/3) = 6250 × 4 = ₹25,000

∴ The correct answer is ₹25,000.

Alternate Method

Given: MPB = ₹35,000, DiscountB = 40%, DiscountA = 25%, SPB − SPA = ₹2,250.

Formula: SP = MP × (100 − Discount)%

⇒ SP of B = 35000 × (100 − 40) / 100

⇒ SP of B = 35000 × 0.60 = ₹21,000

⇒ SP of A = SP of B − 2250

⇒ SP of A = 21000 − 2250 = ₹18,750

⇒ SP of A = MPA × (100 − 25) / 100

⇒ 18750 = MPA × 0.75

⇒ MPA = 18750 ÷ 0.75 = 25000

∴ The correct answer is ₹25,000.

Additional Information

Selling Price and Discount

SP = MP − Discount or SP = MP × (1 − d/100), where d is the discount percentage.

Relationship between MP, CP, and Profit

MP/CP = (100 + Profit%) / (100 − Discount%). This is useful when both profit and discount percentages are given.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts d1 and d2 are given, the single equivalent discount is (d1 + d2 − (d1 × d2)/100)%.

questions.question: If 60% discount is offered on the marked price and selling price becomes equal to cost price then what was the % mark up?
questions.questionHtml: If 60% discount is offered on the marked price and selling price becomes equal to cost price then what was the % mark up?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Assume Marked Price (MP) = 100 units.

Selling Price (SP) = 100 − 60% of 100 = 40 units.

Since SP = CP, then Cost Price (CP) = 40 units.

Markup = MP − CP = 100 − 40 = 60 units.

% Markup = (60 ÷ 40) × 100 = 150%.

∴ The correct answer is 150%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Discount % = 60%

Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price (CP)

Formula Used:

SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

% Markup = [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

⇒ Let MP = 100

⇒ SP = 100 × (100 − 60) ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 100 × 40 ÷ 100 = 40

⇒ Given SP = CP, ∴ CP = 40

⇒ Markup = MP − CP = 100 − 40 = 60

⇒ % Markup = (60 ÷ 40) × 100

⇒ % Markup = 1.5 × 100 = 150%

∴ The correct answer is 150%.

Additional Information

Relation between CP and MP

CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%). If Profit = 0 (i.e., SP = CP), then CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Markup Percentage

It is the percentage by which the cost price is increased to set the marked price. Markup% = (Markup ÷ CP) × 100.

Net Effect Rule

Profit% = Markup% − Discount% − (Markup% × Discount% ÷ 100). In this case, Profit% = 0.

questions.question: If 3A = 6B = 9C, what is A ∶ B ∶ C?
questions.questionHtml: If 3A = 6B = 9C, what is A ∶ B ∶ C?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

If k1A = k2B = k3C, then A ∶ B ∶ C = (k2 × k3) ∶ (k1 × k3) ∶ (k1 × k2).

A ∶ B ∶ C = (6 × 9) ∶ (3 × 9) ∶ (3 × 6)

A ∶ B ∶ C = 54 ∶ 27 ∶ 18

Dividing all terms by 9, we get A ∶ B ∶ C = 6 ∶ 3 ∶ 2.

∴ The correct answer is 6 : 3 : 2.

Alternate Method

Given: 3A = 6B = 9C

Formula: If aA = bB = cC = k, then A = k/a, B = k/b, and C = k/c.

⇒ Let 3A = 6B = 9C = k

⇒ A = k/3, B = k/6, C = k/9

⇒ A ∶ B ∶ C = k/3 ∶ k/6 ∶ k/9

⇒ Finding LCM of denominators (3, 6, 9) = 18

⇒ A ∶ B ∶ C = (1/3 × 18) ∶ (1/6 × 18) ∶ (1/9 × 18)

⇒ A ∶ B ∶ C = 6 ∶ 3 ∶ 2

∴ The correct answer is 6 : 3 : 2.

Additional Information

Reciprocal Ratio Property

When quantities are inversely proportional, such as aA = bB, the ratio A ∶ B is equal to the reciprocal of their coefficients, which is 1/a ∶ 1/b or simply b ∶ a.

Ratio and Constant proportionality

If A/x = B/y = C/z, then the ratio A ∶ B ∶ C is directly x ∶ y ∶ z. In contrast, when the coefficients are multiplied (xA = yB), we must use the LCM method.

Compound Ratio

A compound ratio is found by multiplying the corresponding terms of two or more ratios. For ratios a ∶ b and c ∶ d, the compound ratio is ac ∶ bd.

questions.question: How many job applicants had applied if the ratio of selected to unselected was 19 : 17. If 1,200 less had applied and 800 less selected, then the ratio of selected to unselected would have been 1 : 1.
questions.questionHtml: How many job applicants had applied if the ratio of selected to unselected was 19 : 17. If 1,200 less had applied and 800 less selected, then the ratio of selected to unselected would have been 1 : 1.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Initial Ratio (Total : Selected) = 36 : 19 (since 19 + 17 = 36)

Final Ratio (Total : Selected) = 2 : 1 (since 1 : 1 means 1 out of 2 are selected)

Apply Cross-Product: |(36 × 1) − (19 × 2)| units = |(2 × 800) − (1 × 1200)|

|36 − 38| units = |1600 − 1200| ⇒ 2 units = 400

1 unit = 200 ∴ Initial Total = 36 × 200 = 7200

∴ The correct answer is 7200 applicants.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial Selected : Unselected = 19 : 17

Reduction in Applied = 1200 | Reduction in Selected = 800

Final Selected : Unselected = 1 : 1

Formula Used:

Total Applicants = Selected + Unselected

Let initial Selected = 19x and Unselected = 17x

⇒ Total Applicants = 19x + 17x = 36x

⇒ New Total Applicants = 36x − 1200

⇒ New Selected Applicants = 19x − 800

According to the new ratio (1 : 1), Selected = 1/2 of Total:

⇒ (19x − 800) = 1/2 × (36x − 1200)

⇒ 2 × (19x − 800) = 36x − 1200

⇒ 38x − 1600 = 36x − 1200

⇒ 38x − 36x = 1600 − 1200

⇒ 2x = 400

⇒ x = 200

⇒ Initial Applicants = 36 × 200 = 7200

∴ The correct answer is 7200 applicants.

Additional Information

Compound Ratio

The ratio of the products of the antecedents and the products of the consequents of two or more ratios. For a:b and c:d, it is (ac):(bd).

Componento and Dividendo

If a/b = c/d, then (a+b)/(a-b) = (c+d)/(c-d). This is useful in solving complex ratio equations involving additions or subtractions.

Cross-Multiplication Method

Used when an initial ratio is changed by adding/subtracting specific values to reach a final ratio. It avoids setting up full algebraic equations.

questions.question: What is the third proportional to 10 and 20?
questions.questionHtml: What is the third proportional to 10 and 20?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In a continued proportion a : b :: b : c, the third proportional c is calculated as b2 ÷ a.

Given a = 10 and b = 20.

Third proportional = (20 × 20) ÷ 10 = 400 ÷ 10 = 40.

∴ The correct answer is 40.

Alternate Method

Given: First number (a) = 10, Second number (b) = 20.

Formula Used: If three numbers a, b, and c are in proportion, then a : b = b : c, where c is the third proportional.

⇒ Let the third proportional be c.

⇒ 10 : 20 = 20 : c

⇒ 10 ÷ 20 = 20 ÷ c

⇒ 10 × c = 20 × 20

⇒ 10c = 400

⇒ c = 400 ÷ 10

⇒ c = 40

∴ The correct answer is 40.

Additional Information

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is calculated as x = √(a × b).

Fourth Proportional

For three numbers a, b, and c, the fourth proportional d satisfies a : b = c : d, which gives d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Continued Proportion Property

Three non-zero numbers a, b, and c are in continued proportion if the ratio of the first to the second equals the ratio of the second to the third (a/b = b/c).

questions.question: The ratio of the sum of the salaries of A and B to the difference of their salaries is 11 : 1 and the ratio of the sum of the salaries of B and C to the difference of their salaries is also 11 : 1. If A's salary is the highest and C's is the lowest then what is B's salary (in Rs) given the total of all their salaries is Rs. 1,82,000?
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of the sum of the salaries of A and B to the difference of their salaries is 11 : 1 and the ratio of the sum of the salaries of B and C to the difference of their salaries is also 11 : 1. If A's salary is the highest and C's is the lowest then what is B's salary (in Rs) given the total of all their salaries is Rs. 1,82,000?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

By Componendo & Dividendo, if (S+D)/(S−D) = 11/1, then the ratio of terms is (11+1)/(11−1) = 12/10 = 6/5.

So, A : B = 6 : 5 and B : C = 6 : 5.

Combined ratio A : B : C = (6×6) : (5×6) : (5×5) = 36 : 30 : 25.

Total units = 36 + 30 + 25 = 91 units.

91 units = ₹1,82,000 → 1 unit = ₹2,000.

B's salary = 30 units × 2,000 = ₹60,000.

∴ The correct answer is ₹60,000.

Alternate Method

Given:

(A + B) / (A − B) = 11 / 1

(B + C) / (B − C) = 11 / 1

Total salary (A + B + C) = ₹1,82,000

Formula Used:

Componendo and Dividendo: If a/b = c/d, then (a+b)/(a−b) = (c+d)/(c−d)

Calculations:

From (A + B) / (A − B) = 11 / 1:

⇒ Applying Componendo & Dividendo: ((A + B) + (A − B)) / ((A + B) − (A − B)) = (11 + 1) / (11 − 1)

⇒ 2A / 2B = 12 / 10

⇒ A / B = 6 / 5

Similarly, for B and C:

⇒ B / C = 6 / 5

To combine the ratios, make B common:

⇒ A : B = 6 : 5 = (6 × 6) : (5 × 6) = 36 : 30

⇒ B : C = 6 : 5 = (6 × 5) : (5 × 5) = 30 : 25

⇒ A : B : C = 36 : 30 : 25

Sum of ratio parts:

⇒ 36 + 30 + 25 = 91 units

⇒ 91 units = ₹1,82,000

⇒ 1 unit = 1,82,000 ÷ 91 = ₹2,000

Calculate B’s salary:

⇒ B = 30 × 2,000 = ₹60,000

∴ The correct answer is ₹60,000.

Additional Information

Componendo and Dividendo Rule

It is a theorem on proportions that allows for quick calculation of individual variables when the ratio of their sum and difference is known. If a/b = c/d, then (a+b)/(a−b) = (c+d)/(c−d).

Combined Ratio

When two ratios a : b and b : c are given, the combined ratio a : b : c can be found by making the common term 'b' equal in both ratios through multiplication.

Partitive Proportion

It involves dividing a total amount into parts based on a specific ratio. Value of one part = Total Amount ÷ Sum of Ratio Parts.

questions.question: If by increasing the price of a ticket in the ratio 8 : 11 the number of tickets sold fall in the ratio 23 : 21 then what is the increase (in Rs.) in revenue if revenue before increase in price of ticket was Rs. 36,800?
questions.questionHtml: If by increasing the price of a ticket in the ratio 8 : 11 the number of tickets sold fall in the ratio 23 : 21 then what is the increase (in Rs.) in revenue if revenue before increase in price of ticket was Rs. 36,800?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Revenue Ratio = (Initial Price × Initial Quantity) : (Final Price × Final Quantity)

Revenue Ratio = (8 × 23) : (11 × 21) = 184 : 231

Initial Revenue = 184 units = ₹36,800 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹200

Increase in Revenue = 231 − 184 = 47 units

Required Increase = 47 × 200 = ₹9,400

∴ The correct answer is ₹9400.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial Price : Final Price = 8 : 11

Initial Tickets : Final Tickets = 23 : 21

Initial Revenue = ₹36,800

Formula Used:

Revenue = Price × Number of Tickets Sold

Calculations:

⇒ Let initial price = 8x and initial quantity = 23y

⇒ Initial Revenue = 8x × 23y = 184xy

⇒ Final Price = 11x and final quantity = 21y

⇒ Final Revenue = 11x × 21y = 231xy

⇒ Given: 184xy = 36800

⇒ xy = 36800 ÷ 184 = 200

⇒ Increase in revenue = Final Revenue − Initial Revenue

⇒ Increase = 231xy − 184xy = 47xy

⇒ Increase = 47 × 200 = ₹9,400

∴ The correct answer is ₹9400.

Additional Information

Product of Ratios

When a quantity depends on the product of two independent variables (like Revenue = Price × Quantity), the ratio of the new quantity to the old is the product of the individual ratios of those variables.

Percentage Change in Product

If one factor increases by a% and the other increases by b%, the net percentage change in the product is given by the formula: [a + b + (ab/100)]%.

Compounding Ratios

To find the combined effect of two ratios a:b and c:d, we multiply them as (a×c):(b×d). This is known as compounding the ratios.

questions.question: The ratio of ages of the father and mother was 11 ∶ 10 when their son was born. The ratio of ages of the father and mother will be 19 ∶ 18 when the son will be twice his present age. What is the ratio of present ages of father and mother?
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of ages of the father and mother was 11 ∶ 10 when their son was born. The ratio of ages of the father and mother will be 19 ∶ 18 when the son will be twice his present age. What is the ratio of present ages of father and mother?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio at son's birth (Son = 0) → 11 : 10 (Difference = 1 unit)

Ratio at Son = 2x years → 19 : 18 (Difference = 1 unit)

Since the difference is same, total growth in 2x years = 19 − 11 = 8 units.

Growth for present age (x years) = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 units.

Present ratio = (11 + 4) : (10 + 4) = 15 : 14.

∴ The correct answer is 15 : 14.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial ratio (Son = 0) = 11 : 10

Future ratio (Son = 2 × present age) = 19 : 18

Formula Used:

Age = Initial age + time elapsed

Calculations:

Let the ages of father and mother at son's birth be 11k and 10k.

Let the son's present age be x.

Ages at the time when son will be 2x years old:

Father's age = 11k + 2x

Mother's age = 10k + 2x

⇒ (11k + 2x) ÷ (10k + 2x) = 19 ÷ 18

⇒ 18 × (11k + 2x) = 19 × (10k + 2x)

⇒ 198k + 36x = 190k + 38x

⇒ 198k − 190k = 38x − 36x

⇒ 8k = 2x

⇒ x = 4k

Present ages:

Father = 11k + x = 11k + 4k = 15k

Mother = 10k + x = 10k + 4k = 14k

⇒ Ratio = 15k : 14k = 15 : 14

∴ The correct answer is 15 : 14.

Additional Information

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two people always remains the same, regardless of the number of years passed. In ratio problems, always try to equalize this difference.

Ratio Scaling

If the difference between two ratios a:b and c:d is not the same, multiply (a:b) by (d−c) and (c:d) by (b−a) to make the differences equal.

Linear Increment

When everyone in a group grows by 'n' years, their total age increases by (number of people × n) and the average age increases by exactly n years.

questions.question: Of the 3 numbers whose average is 22, the first is 3/8 th the sum of other two. What is the first number?
questions.questionHtml: Of the 3 numbers whose average is 22, the first is 3/8<sup>th</sup> the sum of other two. What is the first number?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total sum of 3 numbers = 22 × 3 = 66.

Ratio of the 1st number to the sum of the other two = 3 : 8.

Total ratio parts = 3 + 8 = 11 units.

11 units = 66 ⇒ 1 unit = 6.

First number = 3 units = 3 × 6 = 18.

∴ The correct answer is 18.

Alternate Method

Given: Average of 3 numbers = 22.

Condition: 1st number = 3/8 × (Sum of other two).

Formula: Sum = Average × Number of items.

⇒ Let the three numbers be x, y, and z.

⇒ (x + y + z) ÷ 3 = 22

⇒ x + y + z = 22 × 3 = 66

⇒ Given: x = 3/8 × (y + z)

⇒ 8x = 3(y + z) ⇒ (y + z) = 8x/3

⇒ Substitute (y + z) in the sum equation:

⇒ x + 8x/3 = 66

⇒ (3x + 8x) / 3 = 66

⇒ 11x / 3 = 66

⇒ 11x = 198

⇒ x = 198 ÷ 11 = 18

∴ The correct answer is 18.

Additional Information

Definition of Average

Average is the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations. Formula: Average = ∑x / n.

Ratio and Proportion

If a total quantity S is divided into two parts in the ratio a:b, the first part is [a / (a + b)] × S and the second part is [b / (a + b)] × S.

Sum of Observations

The total sum of n observations can always be found by multiplying the average by n. Sum = Average × n.

questions.question: The average of three consecutive odd numbers is 52 more than 1/3 rd of the largest of these numbers. What is the smallest of these numbers?
questions.questionHtml: The average of three consecutive odd numbers is 52 more than 1/3<sup>rd</sup> of the largest of these numbers. What is the smallest of these numbers?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The average of three consecutive odd numbers is the middle number.

Let the middle number be M. The largest number is M + 2.

Given: M = (1/3) × (M + 2) + 52

3M = M + 2 + 156 ⇒ 2M = 158 ⇒ M = 79.

Smallest number = M − 2 = 79 − 2 = 77.

∴ The correct answer is 77.

Alternate Method

Given: Three consecutive odd numbers. The average is 52 more than 1/3rd of the largest number.

Formula Used: Average = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations.

Let the three consecutive odd numbers be x, x + 2, and x + 4.

⇒ Average = (x + x + 2 + x + 4) ÷ 3

⇒ Average = (3x + 6) ÷ 3 = x + 2

According to the problem:

⇒ x + 2 = (1/3) × (x + 4) + 52

⇒ 3(x + 2) = (x + 4) + (52 × 3)

⇒ 3x + 6 = x + 4 + 156

⇒ 3x + 6 = x + 160

⇒ 3x − x = 160 − 6

⇒ 2x = 154

⇒ x = 77

The smallest number is x = 77.

∴ The correct answer is 77.

Additional Information

Average of Consecutive Numbers

For any arithmetic progression with an odd number of terms, the average is exactly the middle term: Average = (First Term + Last Term) ÷ 2.

Properties of Odd Numbers

Consecutive odd numbers always have a common difference of 2. The sum of n consecutive odd numbers starting from 1 is given by n2.

Average Change Rule

If each number in a set is increased by a constant k, the average also increases by k. If multiplied by k, the average is multiplied by k.

questions.question: A batsman scores 98 runs in the 17 th match of his career. His average runs per match increased by 2.5. What is his average before the 17 th match?
questions.questionHtml: A batsman scores 98 runs in the 17<sup>th</sup> match of his career. His average runs per match increased by 2.5. What is his average before the 17<sup>th</sup> match?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total matches played including the current one = 17

Increase in average = 2.5

Total increase in runs across all 17 matches = 17 × 2.5 = 42.5

Old average (Average before 17th match) = Score in 17th match − Total increase

Old average = 98 − 42.5 = 55.5

∴ The correct answer is 55.5.

Alternate Method

Given:

Runs in 17th match = 98

Increase in average = 2.5

Formula:

Average = (Total Runs) ÷ (Number of Matches)

Let the average before 17th match be x.

Total runs after 16 matches = 16x

Total runs after 17 matches = 16x + 98

New average after 17 matches = x + 2.5

⇒ (16x + 98) ÷ 17 = x + 2.5

⇒ 16x + 98 = 17(x + 2.5)

⇒ 16x + 98 = 17x + 42.5

⇒ 17x − 16x = 98 − 42.5

⇒ x = 55.5

∴ The correct answer is 55.5.

Additional Information

New Average Formula

New Average = Old Average + (Increase in Average) = 55.5 + 2.5 = 58.

Weighted Average Concept

If an observation is added, New Sum = (Old Average × Old n) + New Observation. The change in average is (New Observation − Old Average) ÷ New n.

Score Calculation

Score of the nth match = New Average + (n − 1) × (Increase in Average).

∴ The correct answer is 55.5.

questions.question: What is the average of all numbers between 100 and 200 which are divisible by 13?
questions.questionHtml: What is the average of all numbers between 100 and 200 which are divisible by 13?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

First number divisible by 13 after 100 = 13 × 8 = 104.

Last number divisible by 13 before 200 = 13 × 15 = 195.

For any sequence in Arithmetic Progression (AP), Average = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2.

Average = (104 + 195) ÷ 2 = 299 ÷ 2 = 149.5.

∴ The correct answer is 149.5.

Alternate Method

Given: Numbers between 100 and 200 divisible by 13.

Formula Used: Average of Arithmetic Progression = (a + l) ÷ 2

⇒ Multiples of 13 in the range: 13 × 8, 13 × 9, ..., 13 × 15.

⇒ The series is: 104, 117, 130, 143, 156, 169, 182, 195.

⇒ First term (a) = 104.

⇒ Last term (l) = 195.

⇒ Average = (104 + 195) ÷ 2.

⇒ Average = 299 ÷ 2 = 149.5.

∴ The correct answer is 149.5.

Additional Information

Average of AP Sequence

The average of any sequence in Arithmetic Progression is always the arithmetic mean of the first and last terms, i.e., Average = (a + l) ÷ 2.

Number of Terms in AP

The number of terms 'n' can be calculated using n = [(Last Term − First Term) ÷ Common Difference] + 1.

Sum of AP Terms

The sum of terms in an AP is given by Sn = n × Average = (n ÷ 2) × [First Term + Last Term].

questions.question: A vendor buys 9 bananas for Rs. 8 and sells 8 for Rs. 9. What will be the profit or loss (in %)?
questions.questionHtml: A vendor buys 9 bananas for Rs. 8 and sells 8 for Rs. 9. What will be the profit or loss (in %)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use the cross-multiplication method for Article vs Price:

CP: 9 articles for ₹8 | SP: 8 articles for ₹9

Cross-multiply: (9 × 9) − (8 × 8) = 81 − 64 = 17 (Profit units)

Profit % = (Difference ÷ Product of inner values) × 100

Profit % = (17 ÷ 64) × 100 = 26.5625% ≈ 26.56%

∴ The correct answer is 26.56% profit.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost Price (CP) of 9 bananas = ₹8

Selling Price (SP) of 8 bananas = ₹9

To find profit or loss, we equalize the quantity of bananas by taking the LCM of 9 and 8 (LCM = 72).

⇒ CP of 1 banana = 8 ÷ 9

⇒ SP of 1 banana = 9 ÷ 8

⇒ Total CP for 72 bananas = (8 ÷ 9) × 72 = ₹64

⇒ Total SP for 72 bananas = (9 ÷ 8) × 72 = ₹81

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 81 − 64 = ₹17

⇒ Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (17 ÷ 64) × 100 = 26.5625%

∴ The correct answer is 26.56% profit.

Additional Information

Profit and Loss Percentages

Profit % is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless stated otherwise: Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Unitary Method for Articles

When quantities are different, find the price of 1 unit or use the LCM of quantities to make them equal for direct comparison.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP): SP = MP − Discount. Effective profit is then calculated from SP and CP.

questions.question: If a stall sells a pizza at Rs. 200 he makes 20% loss if he wants to make 10% profit then at what price (in Rs.) should he sell?
questions.questionHtml: If a stall sells a pizza at Rs. 200 he makes 20% loss if he wants to make 10% profit then at what price (in Rs.) should he sell?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Direct Ratio: SP1 ÷ (100 − Loss%) = SP2 ÷ (100 + Profit%)

200 ÷ 80 = SP2 ÷ 110

2.5 = SP2 ÷ 110

SP2 = 2.5 × 110 = 275

∴ The correct answer is ₹275.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial Selling Price (SP1) = ₹200

Loss Percentage = 20%

Desired Profit Percentage = 10%

Formula Used:

Cost Price (CP) = SP × 100 ÷ (100 − Loss%)

New Selling Price (SP2) = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

Calculations:

⇒ First, find the Cost Price (CP):

⇒ CP = 200 × 100 ÷ (100 − 20)

⇒ CP = 200 × 100 ÷ 80

⇒ CP = 20000 ÷ 80 = ₹250

⇒ Now, calculate the required Selling Price for 10% profit:

⇒ SP2 = 250 × (100 + 10) ÷ 100

⇒ SP2 = 250 × 110 ÷ 100

⇒ SP2 = 250 × 1.1 = ₹275

∴ The correct answer is ₹275.

Additional Information

Selling Price and Cost Price Relationship

Profit occurs when SP > CP. Profit = SP − CP. Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Loss Calculation

Loss occurs when CP > SP. Loss = CP − SP. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Successive Changes

If an item is sold through multiple hands, the effective change is calculated as: Net SP = Initial CP × (100 ± r1)/100 × (100 ± r2)/100.

questions.question: A wholesaler had 200 dozens of mangoes. He sold some of these mangoes at 20% profit and the rest at 10% profit, so that he made 13% profit on selling all the mangoes. How many mangoes (in dozens) did he sell at 20% profit?
questions.questionHtml: A wholesaler had 200 dozens of mangoes. He sold some of these mangoes at 20% profit and the rest at 10% profit, so that he made 13% profit on selling all the mangoes. How many mangoes (in dozens) did he sell at 20% profit?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Using Alligation Method:

Profit 1 (20%) vs Profit 2 (10%) with Average (13%).

Ratio of quantities = (13 − 10) : (20 − 13) = 3 : 7.

Total units = 3 + 7 = 10 units → 200 dozens.

Mangoes at 20% profit = 3 units = (200 ÷ 10) × 3 = 60 dozens.

∴ The correct answer is 60 dozens.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total quantity = 200 dozens

Profit on first part = 20%

Profit on second part = 10%

Overall profit = 13%

Calculations:

⇒ Let the quantity sold at 20% profit be Q1 and at 10% profit be Q2.

⇒ By Alligation Rule: Q1 : Q2 = (13 − 10) : (20 − 13)

⇒ Q1 : Q2 = 3 : 7

⇒ Total ratio parts = 3 + 7 = 10 units

⇒ 10 units = 200 dozens

⇒ 1 unit = 200 ÷ 10 = 20 dozens

⇒ Quantity at 20% profit = 3 × 20 dozens

⇒ Quantity at 20% profit = 60 dozens

∴ The correct answer is 60 dozens.

Additional Information

Rule of Alligation

It is used to find the ratio in which two ingredients at given prices/percentages must be mixed to produce a mixture at a given mean price/percentage. Formula: (Quantity of Cheaper) / (Quantity of Dearer) = (CP of Dearer − Mean Price) / (Mean Price − CP of Cheaper).

Weighted Average Method

Overall profit percentage can also be calculated as: Pavg = (n1 × p1 + n2 × p2) / (n1 + n2), where n is the quantity and p is the individual profit percentage.

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit % is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless stated otherwise. Profit % = (Profit / CP) × 100.

questions.question: If the selling price is tripled and the cost price is doubled, the profit would become 65%. What is the present profit (in %)?
questions.questionHtml: If the selling price is tripled and the cost price is doubled, the profit would become 65%. What is the present profit (in %)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

New Profit is 65% on doubled CP, so New SP = 165% of (2 × CP).

New SP = 3.3 × CP.

Since New SP is 3 times the original SP, then 3 × Original SP = 3.3 × CP.

Original SP = 1.1 × CP.

Original Profit = 1.1 − 1 = 0.1 = 10%.

∴ The correct answer is 10%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Let original Cost Price = CP and original Selling Price = SP.

New Cost Price (CPnew) = 2 × CP

New Selling Price (SPnew) = 3 × SP

New Profit % = 65%

Formula Used:

SP = CP × (100 + Profit %)/100

Calculations:

⇒ Let CP = 100

⇒ New CP = 2 × 100 = 200

⇒ New SP = New CP × (165/100) = 200 × 1.65

⇒ New SP = 330

⇒ Original SP = New SP ÷ 3

⇒ Original SP = 330 ÷ 3 = 110

⇒ Original Profit = SP − CP = 110 − 100 = 10

⇒ Original Profit % = (10 ÷ 100) × 100 = 10%

∴ The correct answer is 10%.

Additional Information

Profit and Loss Basic Formulas

Profit % = (Profit/CP) × 100 | Loss % = (Loss/CP) × 100. Note that profit and loss are always calculated on Cost Price unless stated otherwise.

Marked Price and Discount

Selling Price = Marked Price − Discount. Discount % is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP).

Relation between CP and MP

CP / MP = (100 − Discount %) / (100 + Profit %). This formula is useful for solving questions involving both discount and profit.

questions.question: 0.06% of 250% of 1600 is _________.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Convert percentages into simple decimal multipliers: 0.06% = 0.0006 and 250% = 2.5.

Expression = 0.0006 × 2.5 × 1600

Multiply 0.0006 by 1600 first: 0.0006 × 1600 = 0.96

Then multiply by 2.5: 0.96 × 2.5 = 2.4

∴ The correct answer is 2.4.

Alternate Method

Given: 0.06% of 250% of 1600

Formula used: x% of y = (x ÷ 100) × y

⇒ Result = (0.06 ÷ 100) × (250 ÷ 100) × 1600

⇒ Result = (6 ÷ 10000) × (2.5) × 1600

⇒ Result = (6 × 2.5 × 1600) ÷ 10000

⇒ Result = (15 × 1600) ÷ 10000

⇒ Result = 24000 ÷ 10000

⇒ Result = 2.4

∴ The correct answer is 2.4.

Additional Information

Percentage to Decimal Rule

To remove the % sign, divide the number by 100 or move the decimal point two places to the left.

BODMAS in Percentages

The word 'of' always indicates a multiplication operation. Successive 'of' operations are solved from left to right or simultaneously as products.

Fraction Equivalents

Using fractions can simplify calculations: 250% = 5/2, while 0.06% = 6/10000 = 3/5000.

questions.question: Two numbers are 90% and 75% lesser than a third number. By what % should the first number be increased so that it becomes equal to the second number?
questions.questionHtml: Two numbers are 90% and 75% lesser than a third number. By what % should the first number be increased so that it becomes equal to the second number?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let the third number be 100.

First number = 100 − 90 = 10

Second number = 100 − 75 = 25

Required percentage increase = [(25 − 10) ÷ 10] × 100

⇒ Required percentage increase = (15 ÷ 10) × 100 = 150%

∴ The correct answer is 150%.

Alternate Method

Given:

First number is 90% lesser than the third number.

Second number is 75% lesser than the third number.

Formula Used:

Percentage Increase = [(Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value] × 100

Calculations:

⇒ Let the third number be x.

⇒ First number = x − 90% of x = 10% of x = 0.10x

⇒ Second number = x − 75% of x = 25% of x = 0.25x

⇒ Increase required for the first number to become equal to the second number = 0.25x − 0.10x = 0.15x

⇒ Percentage increase = (0.15x ÷ 0.10x) × 100

⇒ Percentage increase = 1.5 × 100 = 150%

∴ The correct answer is 150%.

Additional Information

Percentage Change

It is the ratio of the difference between the final and initial values to the initial value, expressed as a percentage. Formula: ((New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value) × 100.

Successive Percentage Change

If a number is successively changed by a% and b%, the net percentage change is given by the formula: a + b + (a × b ÷ 100)%.

Comparing Two Quantities

If quantity A is x% more than quantity B, then B is less than A by a percentage of (x ÷ (100 + x)) × 100.

questions.question: When a number is increased by 216, it becomes 140% of itself. What is the number?
questions.questionHtml: When a number is increased by 216, it becomes 140% of itself. What is the number?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The number becomes 140% of itself, meaning the increase is 40%.

Given that this 40% increase corresponds to the value 216.

40% of Number = 216

100% of Number = (216 ÷ 40) × 100 = 5.4 × 100 = 540

∴ The correct answer is 540.

Alternate Method

Given:

Increase in number = 216

New value = 140% of the original number

Formula Used:

New Value = Original Value + Increase

Calculations:

Let the original number be x.

⇒ x + 216 = 140% of x

⇒ x + 216 = (140 ÷ 100) × x

⇒ x + 216 = 1.4x

⇒ 1.4x − x = 216

⇒ 0.4x = 216

⇒ x = 216 ÷ 0.4

⇒ x = 2160 ÷ 4

⇒ x = 540

∴ The correct answer is 540.

Additional Information

Percentage Increase Formula

Percentage Increase = (Increase ÷ Original Value) × 100. In this case, 40 = (216 ÷ x) × 100.

Fractional Equivalents

40% is equivalent to 2/5. Thus, (2/5) of the number = 216, leading to Number = 216 × 5/2 = 540.

Base Value Concept

In any percentage change problem, the original number is always treated as 100% or the base value 1.

questions.question: A man donates 30% of his wealth to charity. 30% and 25% of the remaining wealth to his wife and son respectively. The rest he divides equally among his three daughters. One of his daughter gets Rs. 42 lakh as her share. What was the man's wealth (in Rs. lakhs)?
questions.questionHtml: A man donates 30% of his wealth to charity. 30% and 25% of the remaining wealth to his wife and son respectively. The rest he divides equally among his three daughters. One of his daughter gets Rs. 42 lakh as her share. What was the man's wealth (in Rs. lakhs)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Remaining wealth after charity = 100% − 30% = 70%.

Total share of Wife and Son from remaining = 30% + 25% = 55%.

Remaining for 3 daughters = 100% − 55% = 45% of the 70% wealth.

Share of one daughter = (45% ÷ 3) × 70% = 15% × 70% = 10.5%.

10.5% = 42 lakh ⇒ 100% = (42 ÷ 10.5) × 100 = 4 × 100 = 400 lakh.

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 400 lakhs.

Alternate Method

Given:

Charity donation = 30% of total wealth.

Wife's share = 30% of remaining wealth.

Son's share = 25% of remaining wealth.

One daughter's share = Rs. 42 lakh (shared equally among 3 daughters).

Formula Used:

Remaining Value = Initial Value × (100 − x)%

Let total wealth be Rs. W lakhs.

⇒ Charity = 0.30 × W

⇒ Remaining Wealth (R1) = W − 0.30W = 0.70W

⇒ Sum of Wife and Son's percentage of R1 = 30% + 25% = 55%

⇒ Rest wealth for daughters = 100% − 55% = 45% of R1

⇒ Total wealth for daughters = 0.45 × 0.70W = 0.315W

⇒ Wealth of one daughter = 0.315W ÷ 3 = 0.105W

⇒ Given: 0.105W = 42

⇒ W = 42 ÷ 0.105

⇒ W = 42000 ÷ 105

⇒ W = 400 lakhs

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 400 lakhs.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Deduction

When multiple deductions are made from the "remaining" amount, use the formula: Final = Initial × (1 − r1/100) × (1 − r2/100).

Simultaneous Deduction from Same Base

If multiple parts (like wife and son) are taken from the same "remaining" base, their percentages are added together before deduction (e.g., 30% + 25% = 55% of the remainder).

Percentage to Ratio Conversion

10.5% can be written as 10.5/100 = 21/200. If 21 units = 42, then 200 units = 400.

questions.question: A bus travels 720 km in 20 hours. Calculate its average speed in meters/second.
questions.questionHtml: A bus travels 720 km in 20 hours. Calculate its average speed in meters/second.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Speed in km/h = 720 ÷ 20 = 36 km/h

Conversion: 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s

Speed in m/s = 36 × (5/18) = 2 × 5 = 10 m/s

∴ The correct answer is 10 m/s.

Alternate Method

Given: Total Distance = 720 km, Total Time = 20 hours

Formula: Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ Average Speed (km/h) = 720 ÷ 20

⇒ Average Speed (km/h) = 36 km/h

⇒ Since 1 km = 1000 m and 1 hour = 3600 s,

⇒ 1 km/h = 1000/3600 m/s = 5/18 m/s

⇒ Speed in m/s = 36 × (5 ÷ 18)

⇒ Speed in m/s = 2 × 5 = 10 m/s

∴ The correct answer is 10 m/s.

Additional Information

Unit Conversion Factor

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed Formula

When a distance is covered at speed 'x' and the same distance is covered back at speed 'y', the average speed for the whole journey is 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Relationship between Speed, Distance, and Time

Speed = Distance ÷ Time | Distance = Speed × Time | Time = Distance ÷ Speed.

questions.question: If a boat goes upstream at a speed of 21 km/h and comes back the same distance at 28 km/h. What is the average speed (in km/hr) for the total journey?
questions.questionHtml: If a boat goes upstream at a speed of 21 km/h and comes back the same distance at 28 km/h. What is the average speed (in km/hr) for the total journey?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When the distance covered is the same for two different speeds, use the harmonic mean formula.

Average Speed = (2 × S1 × S2) ÷ (S1 + S2)

Average Speed = (2 × 21 × 28) ÷ (21 + 28)

Average Speed = 1176 ÷ 49 = 24 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 24 km/h.

Alternate Method

Given: Upstream Speed (u) = 21 km/h, Downstream Speed (v) = 28 km/h.

Formula Used: Average Speed = (Total Distance) ÷ (Total Time)

⇒ Let the distance for one way be the LCM of 21 and 28, which is 84 km.

⇒ Total Distance = 84 + 84 = 168 km

⇒ Time taken (Upstream) = Distance ÷ Speed = 84 ÷ 21 = 4 hours

⇒ Time taken (Downstream) = Distance ÷ Speed = 84 ÷ 28 = 3 hours

⇒ Total Time = 4 + 3 = 7 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 168 ÷ 7 = 24 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 24 km/h.

Additional Information

General Average Speed Formula

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. This applies regardless of whether distances or times are equal.

Boat Speed in Still Water

Boat Speed (x) = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2. In this case, x = (28 + 21) ÷ 2 = 24.5 km/h.

Speed of Stream

Stream Speed (y) = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2. In this case, y = (28 − 21) ÷ 2 = 3.5 km/h.

Average Speed for Equal Time

If time taken for both speeds is equal, Average Speed = (S1 + S2) ÷ 2 (Arithmetic Mean).

questions.question: Two runners A and B start running at 12 km/hr and 16 km/hr towards each other. They meet after 1 hour and 30 minutes. How far (in km) were they from each other when they started?
questions.questionHtml: Two runners A and B start running at 12 km/hr and 16 km/hr towards each other. They meet after 1 hour and 30 minutes. How far (in km) were they from each other when they started?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Relative Speed (towards each other) = Speed A + Speed B = 12 + 16 = 28 km/hr.

Time = 1 hour 30 minutes = 1.5 hours.

Initial Distance = Relative Speed × Time.

Distance = 28 × 1.5 = 42 km.

∴ The correct answer is 42 km.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of runner A (SA) = 12 km/hr

Speed of runner B (SB) = 16 km/hr

Meeting time (T) = 1 hour 30 minutes

Formula:

Total Distance = (Relative Speed) × Time

Calculations:

⇒ Time in hours = 1 + 30/60 = 1.5 hours

⇒ Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = SA + SB

⇒ Relative Speed = 12 + 16 = 28 km/hr

⇒ Distance = 28 × 1.5

⇒ Distance = 28 × 3/2

⇒ Distance = 14 × 3 = 42 km

∴ The correct answer is 42 km.

Additional Information

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move towards each other, relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S1 + S2). If they move in the same direction, it is the difference (S1 − S2).

Distance-Speed-Time Relation

The basic formula is Distance = Speed × Time. To find time, use Time = Distance ÷ Speed.

Unit Conversion

Always ensure units are consistent. To convert minutes to hours, divide by 60. To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18.

questions.question: Flight A usually takes 1 hour more than Flight B to travel a distance of 7200 km. Due to engine trouble, the speed of flight B becomes 5/6 times of its actual speed, so it takes 36 minutes more than Flight A to complete the same journey. What is the speed of Flight A (in km/hr)?
questions.questionHtml: Flight A usually takes 1 hour more than Flight B to travel a distance of 7200 km. Due to engine trouble, the speed of flight B becomes 5/6 times of its actual speed, so it takes 36 minutes more than Flight A to complete the same journey. What is the speed of Flight A (in km/hr)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Speed ratio of B = 1 : 5/6 = 6 : 5

Time ratio of B = 5 : 6 (since distance is constant)

Difference in B's time = 1 unit = 1 hour (initial lead) + 0.6 hours (later lag) = 1.6 hours

Original time of Flight B = 5 units = 5 × 1.6 = 8 hours

Usual time of Flight A = 8 + 1 = 9 hours

Speed of Flight A = 7200 ÷ 9 = 800 km/hr

∴ The correct answer is 800 km/hr.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total Distance = 7200 km

Usual Time difference: TA − TB = 1 hour

New speed of B = 5/6 × Original speed of B

New time difference: T'B − TA = 36/60 hours = 0.6 hours

Formula Used:

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

When distance is constant, Speed1 × Time1 = Speed2 × Time2

Calculations:

⇒ Total change in time for Flight B = (TA + 0.6) − (TA − 1)

⇒ Total change in time for Flight B = 1.6 hours

⇒ Let usual time for B be TB. New time T'B = (6/5) × TB

⇒ T'B − TB = 1.6

⇒ (6/5)TB − TB = 1.6

⇒ (1/5)TB = 1.6

⇒ TB = 1.6 × 5 = 8 hours

⇒ Usual time of Flight A = TB + 1 = 8 + 1 = 9 hours

⇒ Speed of Flight A = 7200 ÷ 9

⇒ Speed of Flight A = 800 km/hr

∴ The correct answer is 800 km/hr.

Additional Information

Speed-Time Relationship

For a fixed distance, speed is inversely proportional to time. If speed becomes x/y of original, time becomes y/x of original.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is the difference between their speeds (S1 − S2).

Average Speed

If a journey is divided into two equal distances with speeds x and y, the average speed is 2xy ÷ (x + y).

questions.question: In how many years will Rs. 2,000 yield Rs. 662 as compound interest at 10% per annum compounded annually?
questions.questionHtml: In how many years will Rs. 2,000 yield Rs. 662 as compound interest at 10% per annum compounded annually?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + CI = 2000 + 662 = ₹2662.

Ratio A : P = 2662 : 2000 = 1331 : 1000.

Rate 10% means a growth factor of 11/10.

Observe that 1331/1000 = (11/10)3.

The power 3 directly indicates the time period.

∴ The correct answer is 3 years.

Alternate Method

Given: Principal (P) = ₹2,000, Compound Interest (CI) = ₹662, Rate (R) = 10% p.a.

Formula Used: Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)n, where n = time in years.

⇒ Amount (A) = P + CI = 2000 + 662 = ₹2662

⇒ 2662 = 2000(1 + 10/100)n

⇒ 2662 / 2000 = (110 / 100)n

⇒ 1331 / 1000 = (11 / 10)n

⇒ (11 / 10)3 = (11 / 10)n

⇒ n = 3 years

∴ The correct answer is 3 years.

Additional Information

Effective Rate of Interest

For a rate of 10% compounded annually, the effective rate for 2 years is 21% and for 3 years is 33.1%.

CI and SI Difference (3 years)

The difference between CI and SI for 3 years is given by D3 = P × (R/100)2 × (3 + R/100).

Compounding Half-Yearly

If interest is compounded half-yearly, the rate becomes R/2 and the time period becomes 2n.

questions.question: What is the compound interest earned on Rs. 80,000 at 40% per annum in 1 year compounded quarterly?
questions.questionHtml: What is the compound interest earned on Rs. 80,000 at 40% per annum in 1 year compounded quarterly?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Quarterly Rate = 40% ÷ 4 = 10%.

Time periods for 1 year = 4 quarters.

Effective interest percentage for 4 cycles of 10% = 46.41%.

Compound Interest = 80,000 × 46.41% = 800 × 46.41 = 37128.

∴ The correct answer is ₹37128.

Alternate Method

Given: Principal (P) = ₹80,000, Annual Rate (R) = 40%, Time (T) = 1 Year.

Formula Used: Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)n, where r = rate per period and n = number of periods.

⇒ Rate per quarter (r) = 40% ÷ 4 = 10%.

⇒ Number of quarters (n) = 1 × 4 = 4.

⇒ Amount (A) = 80,000 × (1 + 10/100)4

⇒ A = 80,000 × (1.1)4

⇒ A = 80,000 × 1.4641 = ₹1,17,128.

⇒ Compound Interest (CI) = Amount − Principal

⇒ CI = 1,17,128 − 80,000 = ₹37,128.

∴ The correct answer is ₹37128.

Additional Information

Effective Rate of Interest

The effective annual rate when compounded n times a year is [(1 + r/n)n − 1] × 100.

Compounding Frequency Rules

For half-yearly, Rate = R/2 and Time = 2T. For quarterly, Rate = R/4 and Time = 4T.

CI and SI Difference (2 Years)

The difference between CI and SI for 2 years is given by the formula P(r/100)2.

questions.question: An investor invested his saving in the stock market. The value of his investments increased by 12% and 9% in the first year and the second year respectively. If the value of his investments after two years became Rs. 97,664 then how much had he invested (in Rs.)?
questions.questionHtml: An investor invested his saving in the stock market. The value of his investments increased by 12% and 9% in the first year and the second year respectively. If the value of his investments after two years became Rs. 97,664 then how much had he invested (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Effective percentage increase = a + b + (a × b)/100

Effective increase = 12 + 9 + (12 × 9)/100 = 21 + 1.08 = 22.08%

Initial investment (100%) = Final value ÷ 122.08%

Investment = (97664 ÷ 122.08) × 100 = 800 × 100 = ₹80000

∴ The correct answer is ₹80000.

Alternate Method

Given:

Rate of increase in Year 1 (R1) = 12%

Rate of increase in Year 2 (R2) = 9%

Final Value after 2 years = ₹97,664

Formula Used:

Final Value = Initial Investment × (1 + R1/100) × (1 + R2/100)

Calculations:

⇒ 97664 = P × (1 + 12/100) × (1 + 9/100)

⇒ 97664 = P × (112/100) × (109/100)

⇒ 97664 = P × (1.12 × 1.09)

⇒ 97664 = P × 1.2208

⇒ P = 97664 ÷ 1.2208

⇒ P = 80000

∴ The correct answer is ₹80000.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Formula

For two successive changes of x% and y%, the net change is given by [x + y + (xy/100)]%.

Compound Growth

Initial Value × Multiplier1 × Multiplier2 = Final Value, where Multiplier = (1 ± r/100).

Reverse Percentage Calculation

To find the original value when a value is increased by k%, divide the final value by (1 + k/100).

questions.question: What is the rate of interest (in %) if simple interest earned on a certain sum for the 3 years is Rs. 6,000 and compound interest earned for 2 years is Rs. 4,160?
questions.questionHtml: What is the rate of interest (in %) if simple interest earned on a certain sum for the 3 years is Rs. 6,000 and compound interest earned for 2 years is Rs. 4,160?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

SI for 1 year = 6000 ÷ 3 = ₹2000.

SI for 2 years = 2000 × 2 = ₹4000.

CI for 2 years = ₹4160.

Difference (Interest on 1st year SI) = 4160 − 4000 = ₹160.

Rate (R%) = (160 ÷ 2000) × 100 = 8%.

∴ The correct answer is 8%.

Alternate Method

Given: Simple Interest (SI) for 3 years = ₹6000, Compound Interest (CI) for 2 years = ₹4160.

Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100; CI for 2 years = 2 × (SI for 1 year) + Interest on SI of 1st year.

⇒ Simple Interest for 1 year = 6000 ÷ 3 = ₹2000

⇒ Simple Interest for 2 years = 2000 × 2 = ₹4000

⇒ Compound Interest for 2 years = ₹4160

⇒ Difference between CI and SI for 2 years = 4160 − 4000 = ₹160

⇒ This difference (₹160) is the interest calculated on the SI of the first year (₹2000) for 1 year.

⇒ Rate of Interest (R) = (Difference × 100) ÷ (SI for 1 year × Time)

⇒ R = (160 × 100) ÷ (2000 × 1)

⇒ R = 16000 ÷ 2000 = 8%

∴ The correct answer is 8%.

Additional Information

Relationship between CI and SI for 2 Years

For a period of 2 years, the ratio of CI to SI is given by CI/SI = (200 + R)/200, where R is the annual rate of interest.

Difference between CI and SI for 2 Years

The difference (D) between CI and SI for 2 years can be calculated using the formula: D = P(R/100)2.

Difference between CI and SI for 3 Years

The difference (D) for 3 years is calculated as: D = [P(R/100)2] × [(300 + R)/100].

Simple Interest Property

Simple interest remains constant for every year if the principal and rate of interest do not change.

questions.question: In the given figure, in ΔSTU, ST = 8 cm, TU = 9 cm and SU = 12 cm. QU = 24 cm, SR = 32 cm and PT = 27 cm. What is the ratio of the area of ΔPQU and area of ΔPTR?
questions.questionHtml: In the given figure, in ΔSTU, ST = 8 cm, TU = 9 cm and SU = 12 cm. QU = 24 cm, SR = 32 cm and PT = 27 cm. What is the ratio of the area of ΔPQU and area of ΔPTR?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

From ΔSTU, using Sine Rule: sin U / sin T = ST / SU = 8 / 12 = 2/3.

Calculate extended segments: PU = PT − TU = 27 − 9 = 18 cm and TR = SR − ST = 32 − 8 = 24 cm.

Area Ratio = (PU × QU × sin U) / (PT × TR × sin T).

Ratio = (18 × 24 × sin U) / (27 × 24 × sin T) = (18 / 27) × (sin U / sin T) = 2/3 × 2/3 = 4/9.

∴ The correct answer is 4 : 9.

Alternate Method

Given: ST = 8 cm, TU = 9 cm, SU = 12 cm, QU = 24 cm, SR = 32 cm, PT = 27 cm.

Formula: Area of a triangle = 1/2 × a × b × sin(θ)

⇒ In ΔSTU, by Law of Sines: ST / sin U = SU / sin T

⇒ sin U / sin T = ST / SU = 8 / 12 = 2/3

⇒ From the figure, P, U, T are collinear: PU = PT − TU = 27 − 9 = 18 cm

⇒ S, T, R are collinear: TR = SR − ST = 32 − 8 = 24 cm

⇒ Area(ΔPQU) = 1/2 × PU × QU × sin U = 1/2 × 18 × 24 × sin U

⇒ Area(ΔPTR) = 1/2 × PT × TR × sin T = 1/2 × 27 × 24 × sin T

⇒ Ratio = [1/2 × 18 × 24 × sin U] / [1/2 × 27 × 24 × sin T]

⇒ Ratio = (18 / 27) × (sin U / sin T) = 2/3 × 2/3 = 4/9

∴ The correct answer is 4 : 9.

Additional Information

Law of Sines

In any triangle, the ratio of a side to the sine of its opposite angle is constant: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C.

Area of Triangle (Sine Formula)

The area of a triangle can be calculated as 1/2 × a × b × sin C, where a and b are side lengths and C is the included angle.

Ratio of Areas of Triangles sharing an Angle

If two triangles share a common vertex and their bases are on the same lines, the ratio of their areas depends on the product of the lengths of the sides forming that angle and the sine of the angle.
